elements.element: Customer owns deliverables created for it.
elements.evidence: Section 10.4 instead provides that writings and works of authorship created by M&I while performing the Services are M&I's property.

elements.element: Customer owns work product created for it.
elements.evidence: The clause assigns ownership of the relevant work product to M&I, even when Customer paid for it.

elements.element: Vendor assigns ownership of the deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: There is no assignment to Customer; the clause expressly reserves ownership to M&I.

elements.element: Vendor retains ownership of its pre-existing IP.
elements.evidence: The added sentence confirms M&I's ownership only of its generic tools and know-how, not the broader category of all pre-existing Vendor IP.

elements.element: Vendor grants Customer a licence to Vendor IP embedded in the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The licence covers Developed Software itself, not Vendor IP embedded in Customer-owned deliverables.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor IP is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Although the Developed Software licence is perpetual, no licence to the required subject—embedded Vendor IP—is granted.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Although the Developed Software licence is irrevocable, no licence to the required subject—embedded Vendor IP—is granted.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Although the Developed Software licence is royalty-free, no licence to the required subject—embedded Vendor IP—is granted.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The clause mentions processing Customer's data but contains no reservation or confirmation of Customer's ownership or other rights in Customer Data.

elements.element: There is no joint ownership.
elements.evidence: The clause makes the relevant programs and Developed Software M&I's sole property, thereby excluding joint ownership of those materials.

elements.element: Vendor owns its generic tools.
elements.evidence: The added sentence expressly states that M&I owns its generic tools.

elements.element: Vendor owns its know-how.
elements.evidence: The added sentence expressly states that M&I owns its know-how.

elements.element: Customer receives a licence to the deliverables.
elements.evidence: M&I expressly grants Customer a licence to the Developed Software, which is defined as writings and works of authorship created while performing the Services.

elements.element: The licence is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The licence is expressly described as perpetual.

elements.element: The licence is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The licence is expressly described as irrevocable.

elements.element: The licence is worldwide.
elements.evidence: The licence is expressly described as worldwide.

elements.element: The licence is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The licence is expressly described as royalty-free.

elements.element: Customer may use the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The licence expressly permits Customer to use the Developed Software.

elements.element: Customer may modify the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The licence expressly permits Customer to modify the Developed Software.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The licence expressly permits Customer to sublicense the Developed Software.

elements.element: Customer may exercise the licensed rights for its business.
elements.evidence: The licensed rights are expressly granted for Customer's business.

result.reason: The added sentence supplies every express component of the fallback while leaving the ownership and refund/credit provisions unchanged. It does not satisfy the preferred position because Customer receives no ownership or assignment, no rights in Customer Data, and no licence specifically covering embedded Vendor IP. The drafting also creates facial tension with Section 17.2, which states that Customer has no rights in M&I-provided software or related materials beyond term-limited use to process its data; an express carveout or notwithstanding clause is advisable to ensure the perpetual modification and sublicensing rights are effective.
